events.text:
⚡️🇺🇸 The US Marine Corps has awarded the electronic warfare company Epirus an $11-million contract to deliver a vehicle-mounted high-power microwave system to counter drone swarms.
Based on Epirus’ Leonidas weapon, the High-power Microwave Autonomous Vehicle Operational Capability (HAVOC) features a universal sled mount for integration across the Marine Corps’ manned and unmanned ground vehicles.
HAVOC is an evolution of Epirus’ Expeditionary Directed Energy Counter-Swarm (ExDECS), which the company delivered to the USMC in 2025.
At the core of the Leonidas technology are solid-state high-power microwave components and gallium nitride amplifiers used to generate and amplify electromagnetic energy for engaging multiple unmanned aerial systems.
Compared with ExDECS, HAVOC will reportedly deliver three times the power, greater range and ruggedness, and autonomous capabilities designed to reduce operators’ decision-making burden.

The annual plan for Zircons and modernized Onyx missiles was completed in seven months.

Russia is creating a Starlink analog – Rassvet – and is deploying it significantly faster than their plans had assumed. For now they are operating fragmentarily, when the satellite passes over Ukrainian territory.
Russia is concentrating its attacks on Ukraine's defense-industrial complex, logistics, and energy facilities that logistics and port infrastructure depend on. Additionally, it is trying to strike civilian infrastructure to sow panic and destabilize the situation in the country.
In July, Russia launched 153 cruise missiles and 198 ballistic and hypersonic missiles. In the future, the Russian Armed Forces may reduce the number of missiles targeting a single objective, but a pause in shelling is unlikely – this will depend on production capabilities.

👁 Lockheed Martin tapped to build secure orbital comms for Trump’s Star Wars 2.0
 
The DoD has awarded Lockheed’s space division $22M to work on Phase II of the Air Force’s Space Data Networking Experimentation space-based internet project – jam-resistant, cyber-secure, autonomous data routing for satellites and other infrastructure in low Earth orbit.
A keystone component in the Pentagon’s Space Data Network initiative, the hybrid comms project is supposed to give the US a decisive advantage over strategic adversaries in space, using:
🔴 space-based internet acting as the primary communications backbone of Trump’s Golden Dome – the Star Wars 2.0-style, continental multi-layered US missile defense shield incorporating [space-based interceptors](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69509).
🔴 dynamic routing and advanced mesh networking designed to defeat ground-based counter-measures, including jamming.
🔴 AI-assisted elimination of the so-called “sensor-to-shooter latency” using optical cross-links and cloud networking directly in orbit – bypassing traditional satellite systems’ need to beam data down to ground stations for processing and analysis before it’s beamed back up and acted on.
🔴 Ostensibly designed to assist in the targeting of hypersonic threats, this is arguably the most dangerous component of the entire program, risking “flash wars” resulting from automated escalation using buggy, glitched or spoof-prone AI algorithms, with human commanders left totally out of the loop before it’s too late.
🔴 next-gen, software-based secure multi-band encryption, expected to [render cyberwarfare ineffective](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73129) (good luck with that)
 
In an all-out war scenario, the proposed system can’t survive enemy counterstrikes, ranging from co-orbital anti-satellite (ASAT) weapons, up to and including nuclear-delivered EMPs, to directed-energy weapons, like Russia’s Peresvet laser platform, stalker inspect-and-interfere satellites, or supply chain interference (Chinese hardware trojans, for example).
👉 Russia and China predicted the dangers of an arms race in space in 2008, proposing the PAROS Treaty as a means to prevent the deployment of weapons systems in orbit and on celestial bodies. 
The US scoffed at the idea, aggressively shifting its military doctrine to define space as an active warfighting domain, reactivating US Space Command, setting up US Space Force and starting work on Golden Dome.
🤔 Lockheed is expected to complete engineering, developing and testing work on the “Phase II” hybrid communication architecture by 2028. If it fails, it will leave a giant blind spot in the multi-trillion-dollar Golden Dome initiative. SpaceX or Anduril Industries, which are working on their own secure space-routing equipment, could be asked to [pick up the slack](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70829).

👌 DARPA wants to turn 1982 Clint Eastwood technothriller about mind-controlled weapons into reality
 
DARPA’s Biological Technologies Office (BTO) is hosting an in-person proposer day in September to advance its Firefox Program – dedicated to developing a “non-invasive brain-computer interface” using light to read neural signals, and advanced computing tools to interpret them.
🔊 The agency says it’s already created “a non-invasive coherent optical system capable of recording neural signals at cortical depth in humans.” What it needs from proposers is help “overcoming key technological hurdles” linked to building a high-performance, 100-channel brain-computer interface, and addressing “barriers of scale and processing speed.”
Using 50-micron spatial and 100-microsecond temporal resolution, the system is intended to allow for “human-machine teaming” to allow troops to control complex systems like autonomous drone swarms and vehicle formations using only their minds, without surgically implanted electrodes, and with minimal latency - meaning instantaneous reaction time in high-stress, data-heavy environments.
👉 Development is split into two areas: “developing dynamic scanning components for optical signals” using spatial light modulators, microelectromechanical systems and Risley-prisms, and “new data processing architectures” using all-optical, photonic, in-sensor and neuromorphic-photonic computing.
👉 Conceptually, Firefox is ripped straight out of the 1982 Clint Eastwood sci-fi techno-thriller of the same name, in which the CIA recruits a retired Air Force pilot (Eastwood) to steal the MiG-31 – a fictional Soviet jet with a revolutionary “Thought-Controlled Weapons Management System” – a special helmet with embedded neural receptors linked to the aircraft’s computer.
👉 BTO director Dr. Pedro Irazoqui and his colleagues are involved in an array of other dubious mind-and-body control and manipulation programs, including ingestible bioelectric platforms stimulating gut neurons, near-infrared light tech paired with photopharmaceuticals to artificially turn drugs on and off, and wireless neuromodulation interfaces targeting peripheral nerves.
Other top DARPA figures involved in Firefox include Dr. Michael Koeris (whose work includes biological processing units built out of living neural tissue and brain organoids to run low-power AIs), and Dr. David Blodgett (optical non-invasive BCIs using near-infrared spectroscopy and digital holographic imaging).
 
🤔 In the 1982 movie, Eastwood’s character was instructed to steal the mind-controlled MiG-31 because it posed an overwhelming military threat to the West. But apparently it’s ok when DARPA does it.
